reviewScope: Actual review of eight independent linked-list contracts, forty language algorithm bodies, correctness arguments, traces, distinct reference algorithms, identity observations and property graders. Standalone executions are separate from live website integration.

questions.algorithm: Track seen integer values and bypass later occurrences while retaining the last kept predecessor.
questions.review: All languages keep original first-occurrence nodes in order, preserve every payload and do not delete caller-owned C++ nodes. The grader checks exact retained original IDs rather than accepting copied nodes.
questions.complexity: Expected linear hash-set time; O(u) auxiliary storage for distinct values. Conservative hash-collision worst-case caveat is explicit.

questions.algorithm: Reject nonpositive k, advance lead k links with a null bound, then move lead and follower together.
questions.review: All five return the original selected node, including repeated values; out-of-range and extreme signed 32-bit k return null in bounded time. The JSON index is explicitly an adapter observation rather than the return type.

questions.algorithm: For a nonnull non-tail target, copy its successor value and bypass the successor; otherwise return false.
questions.review: Only the target's Value and Next may change. Snapshots retain the bypassed successor object and verify its fields. The input head and target index never enter the submitted method's argument list.

questions.algorithm: Detach original nodes and append them to smaller and greater-or-equal lists, then join.
questions.review: The implemented order is stable, but the exercise and grader permit unstable valid outputs. Equal-to-pivot nodes may mix with larger nodes. Every original identity must occur exactly once, payloads remain unchanged, and cycles or cloned nodes fail.

questions.algorithm: Reverse order uses direct pointer traversal and an appended result; forward order uses digit stacks and prepends each computed digit.
questions.review: Both publicly implemented digit orders are supported in every language. Per-column totals never exceed 19, so thousands of operand digits never overflow a fixed-width aggregate. New result nodes are disjoint from both preserved operands. Empty/zero and final-carry rules are explicit.
questions.complexity: O(n+m) time. Reverse-order auxiliary space is constant excluding output; forward-order stacks require O(n+m) auxiliary space.

questions.algorithm: Copy values into an auxiliary sequence and compare mirrored positions.
questions.review: No list fields are written on either success or early failure. The stated O(n) auxiliary space matches the actual five implementations; no constant-space reversal claim is made.

questions.algorithm: Two pointers switch to the other head after null, aligning their routes before comparing original-node identity.
questions.review: Private equal-valued prefixes remain separate objects; the common suffix is allocated once. The proof accounts for the null-to-other-head switch step. Return identity and complete graph preservation are graded independently of payload equality.

questions.algorithm: Floyd collision detection, then reset one pointer to the head and advance both equally to the entry.
questions.review: The returned object is the entry, not an arbitrary collision or boolean. All language comparisons use object/pointer identity. Self-cycles, head cycles, acyclic equal payloads, long prefixes and preserved Next fields are covered.

languageBindingReview.csharp: Nullable references and justified nonnull assertions follow the pointer invariants. Forward-mode scan/carry locals have their own names, avoiding C# scope conflicts. HashSet<int> keys are values; dictionary node IDs use the bank model's reference identity.
languageBindingReview.javascript: Set stores integer payloads for deduplication, while Map and strict object comparisons record identities. Math.floor performs carry division. Intermediate arithmetic is at most 19 in addition, with no whole-number conversion.
languageBindingReview.python: Node comparisons use is/is not. A set of values serves deduplication, separate from object-key identity observations. Carry uses integer // division. Node construction and output traversal preserve the declared input graph.
languageBindingReview.cpp: Pointers are passed by value, original nodes remain owned by the adapter, and no input node is deleted. Reverse addition uses a stack-local dummy with new output nodes; forward addition uses vectors as stacks. All candidate results are observed before adapter cleanup.
languageBindingReview.java: All node equality tests compare references. The palindrome implementation explicitly unboxes Integer values before comparison, avoiding cached-box identity errors. ArrayDeque supplies forward-addition stacks; reflection invokes only the submitted callable with its stated arguments.
